text.p: SoftNet Systems Inc said it had revised its previously reported results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended September 30, 1996.

The company said it had increased its provision for the loss on the sale of the Chicago-based non-application oriented interconnect business by $700,000 or $0.10 per share due to the shutdown by the buyer after the year-end.

The increased provision was for the note receivable due from the buyer and the write-off of certain leasehold improvements, the company said. The loss has been presented as extraordinary in the revised results, the company said.

As a result of the revision, the company said it now reports a net loss of $0.05 per share instead of a net profit of $0.05 per share for the fourth quarter, and a net loss of $1.05 per share for the year instead of a loss of $0.83 per share, as reported earlier.
(All data above 000s except per share numbers)

NOTE: For Q4 1996, income from continuing operations was $0.11 per share compared with a loss of $1.37 per share in the prior year period. For the 1996 fiscal year, loss from continuing operations was $0.01 per share verus loss of $1.97 per share in the prior year.
